Candidate set for the extreme-value threshold \(C_{EV}\)

Source: R/em_candidates.R
em_c_candidates.Rd

Builds the set of values over which the EM driver profiles the log-likelihood for the extreme-value threshold \(C_{EV}\): the unique observed response values inside c.lim, optionally thinned.

Usage

em_c_candidates(y, c.lim, prune.c.range)

Arguments

y

Numeric response vector.

c.lim

Length-2 numeric giving the lower and upper bound of the search.

prune.c.range

FALSE for no thinning, or a number in [0, 1] giving the proportion of interior candidates to drop (sampled with probability proportional to the gaps between consecutive candidates, so the endpoints are always kept).

Value

A sorted numeric vector of candidate \(C_{EV}\) values.

Details

This is the ECME step of the algorithm in Appendix A1 of Randahl and Vegelius (2024): \(C_{EV}\) is updated by a grid search over the observed support rather than by a smooth optimiser. A warning is emitted when the set has more than 100 elements and no pruning was requested, because each extra candidate is one extra full-data log-likelihood evaluation per EM iteration.

See also

evzinb(), evinb()
